title: In a second fly connectome (male CNS v1.0), signed wiring from photoreceptors predicted the measured ON or OFF sign of 18 of 24 visual cell types; the same four types were wrong in both animals
abstract: We repeated a parameter-free sign rule from a FlyWire study (sci:5916130f) in a second animal, the male CNS v1.0 connectome. Photoreceptors are ON. Each cell type gets the sign of its summed input, weighted by input synapse fraction. Acetylcholine is excitatory. GABA, glutamate and histamine are inhibitory. We wrote the test plan before we computed any male CNS prediction. Measured signs come from 0.1 Hz full-field flicker calcium responses (Currier and Clandinin 2025). In the right optic lobe, the rule gave the correct sign for 18 of 24 clear types (0.75). A transmitter-label permutation gave mean accuracy 0.45 and one-sided p = 0.029. The left optic lobe also gave 18 of 24. On the 18 types of the FlyWire study, the male CNS gave 13 correct, against 14 in FlyWire. If glutamate was excitatory, accuracy fell to 0.42. TmY14, Dm15, Tm5b and Dm13 were wrong in all four optic lobes of the two animals. Their input structure was the same in both connectomes. The two connectomes predicted the same sign for 83% of 622 matched optic-lobe types, against 52% expected by chance. Limitations: 24 types, moderate p values, one activity data set shared with the earlier study, full-field calcium measurements, and a linear steady-state model. A denominator that included untraced fragments gave 16 of 24.
